# Esther Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 456r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** And it was [vayehi] in the days of Ahasuerus [Achashverosh] — he was the Ahasuerus who reigned from India [Hoddu] unto Ethiopia [Kush], one hundred and twenty-seven provinces [medinot] —

**1:2** in those days, when King [melekh] Ahasuerus sat upon the throne [kisse] of his kingdom [malkhut], which was in Susa [Shushan] the citadel [habirah],

**1:3** in the third year of his reign, he made a feast [mishteh] for all his officials [sarav] and his servants [avadav] — the army [chel] of Persia [Paras] and Media [Madai], the nobles [hapartemim] and the officials [sarei] of the provinces [medinot] before him —

**1:4** when he showed the riches [osher] of the glory [kavod] of his kingdom [malkhuto] and the splendor [yeqar] of the beauty [tiferet] of his greatness [gedulato], many days — one hundred and eighty days.

**1:5** And when these days were fulfilled, the king made for all the people [ha'am] who were found in Susa the citadel, from the great [gadol] unto the small [qatan], a feast [mishteh] of seven days, in the court [chatzer] of the garden [ginat] of the palace [bitan] of the king.

**1:6** White cotton [chur] and blue-violet [tekhelet] hangings, held by cords of fine linen [butz] and purple [argaman] upon silver [kesef] rods [gelilei] and pillars [ammudei] of marble [shesh]; couches [mittot] of gold [zahav] and silver upon a pavement [ritzpat] of alabaster [bahat] and marble [shesh] and mother-of-pearl [dar] and black marble [sokharet].

**1:7** And the drinking [vehashqot] was in vessels [bikhlei] of gold [zahav], and the vessels differed from one vessel to another, and royal [malkhut] wine [yeyn] was abundant [rav], according to the hand [keyad] of the king.

**1:8** And the drinking was according to the law [kaddat] — no one was compelled [ein ones], for so the king had established [yissad] upon every chief steward [rav] of his house, to do according to the desire [kirtzon] of each man [ish va'ish].

**1:9** Also Vashti [Vashti] the queen [hamalkah] made a feast [mishteh] for the women [nashim] in the royal house [beit hamalkhut] which belonged to King Ahasuerus.

**1:10** On the seventh day, when the heart [lev] of the king was merry [tov] with wine [bayyayin], he said to Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas — the seven eunuchs [sarisim] who served [hamsharetim] the face [penei] of King Ahasuerus —

**1:11** to bring Vashti the queen before the king with the royal crown [keter malkhut], to show the peoples [ha'ammim] and the officials [hasarim] her beauty [yofyah], for she was good [tovat] of appearance [mareh].

**1:12** But Queen Vashti refused [vatemmaen] to come at the word [bidvar] of the king which was by the hand of the eunuchs, and the king was exceedingly angry [vayiqtzof], and his wrath [vachamato] burned [ba'arah] within him.

**1:13** And the king said to the wise men [lachakahmim] who knew the times [ha'ittim] — for thus was the matter [devar] of the king before all who knew law [dat] and judgment [din] —

**1:14** and the nearest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan — the seven officials [sarei] of Persia and Media who saw the face [penei] of the king, who sat first [hayyoshevim rishonah] in the kingdom [bamalkhut]:

**1:15** "According to law [kedat], what is to be done with Queen Vashti, because she did not do [lo asetah] the command [ma'amar] of King Ahasuerus by the hand of the eunuchs?"

**1:16** And Memucan said before the king and the officials, "Not against the king alone has Queen Vashti done wrong [avtah], but against all the officials and against all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

**1:17** For the word [devar] of the queen will go out to all the women, to make their husbands [ba'aleihen] despised [livzot] in their eyes, when it is said, 'King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, and she did not come.'

**1:18** And this day the noble women [sarot] of Persia and Media who have heard the word of the queen will say it to all the officials of the king, and there will be enough [kedai] contempt [vizayon] and wrath [qatzef].

**1:19** If it is good [tov] upon the king, let a royal word [devar malkhut] go out from before him, and let it be written [veyikkatev] in the laws [bedatei] of Persia and Media, and let it not pass away [velo ya'avor], that Vashti shall not come before King Ahasuerus, and let the king give her royal position [malkhutah] to her companion [li're'utah] who is better [hattovah] than she.

**1:20** And the decree [pitgam] of the king which he shall make shall be heard [venishma] in all his kingdom — for it is great [rabbah] — and all the wives [hannashim] will give honor [yeqar] to their husbands [leva'aleihen], from the great unto the small."

**1:21** And the word [haddavar] was good [vayyitav] in the eyes of the king and the officials, and the king did according to the word of Memucan.

**1:22** And he sent letters [sefarim] to all the provinces of the king, to each province [medinah] according to its script [kikhtvah] and to each people [am va'am] according to its tongue [kilshono], that every man [ish] should be ruler [sorer] in his house and speak according to the tongue of his people.

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **The Name of God:** The book of Esther is unique among the books of the Hebrew Bible in that the divine name YHWH does not appear anywhere in its text. Nor does the common noun for God [Elohim] appear. This has been a matter of considerable discussion among Jewish and Christian interpreters. EMET preserves the text as received in the Leningrad Codex without interpolation.

2. **Achashverosh (1:1):** Commonly identified with Xerxes I of Persia (486-465 BCE). The Hebrew form [Achashverosh] reflects the Old Persian *Xshayarsha*. The 127 provinces [medinot] describe the administrative structure of the Achaemenid Empire.

3. **Keter malkhut (1:11):** The "royal crown" — the specific term [keter] is a Persian loanword, used frequently in Esther but rarely elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible, reflecting the Persian court setting of the narrative.

4. **Dat (1:13, 1:15, 1:19):** Another Persian loanword meaning "law" or "decree," distinct from the standard Hebrew [torah] or [mishpat]. Its repeated use anchors the narrative firmly in Persian legal and administrative culture.

*— EMET*
